{{for|the ball used in hurling|sliotar}}
'''Donald Solitar''' (September 5, 1932 in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York (state)|New York]], United States – April 28, 2008 in [[Toronto]], Canada) was an American and Canadian mathematician, known for his work in [[combinatorial group theory]].<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor|id=Solitar|title=Donald Solitar}}</ref><ref name="cms">{{citation|title=Professor Donald Solitar|url=http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/history/Obits2/Solitar.html|publisher=[[Canadian Mathematical Society]]|first1=Bob|last1=Burns|first2=Israel|last2=Kleiner|first3=Alfred|last3=Pietrowski|access-date=2014-08-24}}. Reprinted as {{citation|title=Donald M. Solitar *55|journal=Princeton Alumni Weekly|date=July 15, 2009|url=https://paw.princeton.edu/issues/2009/07/15/sections/memorials/4925/index.xml}} and as {{citation|title=Professor Donald Solitar, renowned mathematician|date=May 13, 2008|url=http://yfile.news.yorku.ca/2008/05/13/professor-donald-solitar-renowned-mathematician/|journal=YFile|publisher=York University|access-date=August 25, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826120743/http://yfile.news.yorku.ca/2008/05/13/professor-donald-solitar-renowned-mathematician/|archive-date=August 26, 2014|url-status=dead}}.</ref> The [[Baumslag–Solitar group]]s are named after him and [[Gilbert Baumslag]], after their joint 1962 paper on these groups.

==Life==
Solitar competed on the mathematics team of [[Brooklyn Technical High School]] with his future co-author Abe Karrass, one year ahead of him in school. He graduated from [[Brooklyn College]] in 1953 (with the assistance of tutoring from Karrass, who went to [[New York University]]) and went to [[Princeton University]] for graduate study in mathematics. However, his intended mentor there, [[Emil Artin]], was no longer interested in [[group theory]], so he left with a master's degree and earned his doctorate from [[New York University]] instead, in 1958, under the supervision of [[Wilhelm Magnus]].<ref name="mactutor"/><ref name="cms"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=11649}}</ref>

After finishing his studies, he joined the faculty of [[Adelphi University]] in 1959, and Karrass soon joined him there as a doctoral student, earning a Ph.D. under Solitar's supervision in 1961; this was the first Ph.D. awarded at Adelphi. Karrass remained on the faculty with Solitar, where they founded a summer institute for high school mathematics teachers. Solitar moved to [[New York University Polytechnic School of Engineering|Polytechnic University]] in 1967, and then (as department chair) to [[York University]] in 1968, along with Karrass.<ref name="mactutor"/><ref name="cms"/>

Solitar married J. Francien Hageman, a [[Dutch people|Dutch]] woman, in 1976. He died of a heart attack on April 28, 2008.<ref name="mactutor"/><ref name="cms"/>
